newsitem.title: USA: Peru crisis isolated event, outlook steady - Merrill.
newsitem.headline: Peru crisis isolated event, outlook steady - Merrill.

text.p: Peru's hostage crisis may dent near-term economic expectations, but its recovery in 1997 should remain relatively on course, Merrill Lynch said in a report Tuesday.
Merrill revised down its year-average 1997 growth forecast for Peru to 4.5 percent from 5.4 percent, due to some near-term loss of confidence from the ongoing crisis.
But Merrill left unchanged its long-term outlook.
"Our long-term outlook is unchanged because we view the hostage crisis as an isolated event, not a return to the 1980s," the report said.
Analysts at Merrill noted the hostage crisis may result in some delays or cancellations of private spending, but primarily on smaller projects.

"While large foreign direct investment projects are unlikely to be affected, potential small and medium-sized projects could fail to materialize as a result of an increase in perceived country risk," the report said.

On December 17, the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels stormed the residence of the Japanese ambassador in Lima, taking some 500 hostages and initially threatening to shoot them if 400 jailed colleagues were not freed.
The guerrillas continue to hold over 80 hostages and said today they were not prepared to relax their demands.
But Merrill said the "hostage effect" on confidence could largely disappear within a few months.
A number of factors are expected to support Peru's economic recovery, Merrill said. Among them:

* GDP numbers are likely to be quite strong in coming months -- probably well beyond market expectations -- providing a strong, positive shock to confidence which could offset the negative impact of the crisis.
* Foreign exchange and interest rates have remained stable so far, indicating that locals are not panicking.
* Fiscal and monetary policy is expected to be more supportive of domestic demand next year.
